class: A liveness or health state that is refreshed by ANY inbound traffic on a connection (heartbeats, pings, keep-alive bytes) reports the data stream as live after the data itself has stopped; the connection is alive, the data is not, and the screen shows Connected indefinitely.
mechanism: Kite's ticker sends 1-byte heartbeats about once a second whatever is subscribed; FeedState.on_activity refreshed the last-activity time for heartbeats too, and phase() read health() off that time, so after one price frame the live-market-data row stayed 'healthy' with zero subscriptions and no price frame.

first_seen.where: backend/ofo/marketdata/feed_health.py:62-86, kite_provider.py:76-80 (builder sequence row 2, REQ-015 AC-4, head af331fe4)
first_seen.evidence: verifier probe hb_probe.py: one price frame, unsubscribe, 70 s of heartbeats only -> phase healthy, health AVAILABLE; live GET /api/broker/status 11:47:45 IST with no screen open -> live_market_data connected (orchestrator reading 11:44: still connected 70 s after the last screen closed).

fix: Keep the last PRICE-frame time separately (updated only by data frames) and judge 'live data' from it; heartbeats prove only that the connection is up. A connection with nothing subscribed is its own state (idle), not live and not broken.

detection.note: Fixed in row 2 fix round 1 (8a23776f): FeedState keeps the last price-frame time apart; residual ~3 s from unwanted ticks is issue #513.

occurrences.where: live API on the owner's session, /api/broker/status
occurrences.evidence: connected with no subscription and no price frame for 70 s
